caption:
No one knows what colours Jupiter.

Jupiter’s gas is mostly hydrogen and helium, which look clear in the cold.
Trace gases may paint the clouds. Ammonium hydrosulfide is one guess.
Light clouds ride higher than dark ones and cast thin shadows.

What the astronomers say: light clouds are usually higher than dark ones, and the cause of the colours is still open.

NASA picture: JPL, PIA24972 (JunoCam, colour boosted by citizen scientist Brian Swift). It shows another view of Jupiter’s clouds, taken in 2021.
